title: Anacaona, Taino cacica of Xaragua
summary: Anacaona, a Taino cacica, succeeded her brother Bohechio as ruler of Xaragua in western Hispaniola. In 1503 Governor Nicolas de Ovando campaigned against Xaragua; accounts based on Las Casas say its leaders were seized and many killed, and she was hanged. The region's Taino were then gathered under Spanish supervision.

uncertainty.note: Birth year is an approximation listed by one source only; death in 1503 is given by three sources, and one blog dates the killings to about 29 September 1503.

where.modern_name: Western Hispaniola, Haiti (pin is Leogane, used for the Xaragua heartland)
where.historical_name: Xaragua (Jaragua), a Taino cacicazgo of western Hispaniola

importance.justification: Last independent Taino ruler of Xaragua; her fate marks the end of Taino polities on Hispaniola.

audience_note: Describes the killing of Taino leaders and a public hanging.

sources.title: Contested Conquests: African Maroons and the Incomplete Conquest of Hispaniola, 1519-1620
1503: Anacaona and the caciques of Xaragua

reviewer_note: Birth year (1474) rests on one non-scholarly page and is approximate. The narrative of the killings follows Las Casas as relayed by secondary pages; the place and manner of her execution are not confirmed on the scholarly page, which says only that Ovando defeated her. The pin is a proxy for Xaragua, not a confirmed seat.
